_comment: Worked example: three directives, three failure modes, three contracts.
Copy to <repo-root>/.artifact-gate.json and adapt. The families are independent —
delete the ones you don't run. Every `message` is the text an agent sees at the
moment it is blocked, so it is worth writing them as instructions, not scoldings.

families._comment: A feature/implementation directive. Failure mode: DESIGN steps get skipped, because thinking produces nothing observable.
families.name: feature

gates.message:
Step 4 (design) produced no artifact.

Run the design step and write its output there:
  /rubber-duck                 — walk the logic, surface edge cases
  /grilling                    — attack the design BEFORE it is code
  /skills-from-the-artificer   — which laws apply (Hyrum, Gall, Conway)

Required sections: Behavior table (one row per input class — the row SET is the deliverable) · Negative space (what legitimately looks like your trigger condition and must NOT fire) · Blast radius · Laws that apply · Rejected alternatives · Known limits.

A design step that produces nothing is indistinguishable from a design step that was skipped.

Step 5 (QA matrix) produced no artifact.

Write the enumerated matrix first: one row per INPUT CLASS, categories happy / boundary (limit-1, limit, limit+1) / negative / hostile / independence.

Enumerating the input space on paper is what catches the classes that reach CI otherwise — valid-JSON-that-is-not-an-object, a lone `---` that is a horizontal rule, the CRLF variant. Writing tests for the code you just wrote finds none of them.

Step 6 (orthogonal review) produced no artifact.

Run BOTH engines and record findings + dispositions:
  /code-review       — correctness, logic, edge cases (the named skill, not an ad-hoc agent)
  /security-review   — injection, secrets, traversal, unsafe argv
  at least one in an isolated reviewer context that did not author the change

Shape: {"engines":[{"name":"code-review","isolated":false,"findings":[{"severity":"","summary":"","disposition":""}]}]}

This replaces a self-attestation token with something checkable: such a token asserts the reviews happened, which is exactly the claim that cannot be verified.

families._comment: An unattended bug-sweep directive. Failure modes: stopping at 'PR opened', and silently dropping the rest of the queue after one hard issue.
families.name: bugfix

gates.message:
Diagnosis produced no artifact.

A fix written before the root cause is written down is a guess with a diff attached.

Required sections: Reproduction (exact command + observed output) · Root cause (`file:line`, located not suspected) · Introduced by · Blast radius · Must-Have Acceptance Checklist (verbatim from the issue) · Not-the-bug negative space (what legitimately looks like this symptom and must keep working) · Rejected fixes.

The last two pay for themselves: without negative space you ship an over-broad fix, and a fix with no rejected alternative was not chosen — it was the first thing that came to mind.

QA matrix produced no artifact.

Row 1 is the failing-first regression test, and its `RED proven (sha)` cell carries the run where it actually failed. "The test failed first" is a claim; the sha is evidence.
Two orthogonal reviews, at least one isolated, recorded with a disposition per finding. `not-a-defect` requires the proof, not the assertion.

gates._comment: Contents-checked, not presence-checked. This is where merge policy stops being prose.
gates.message:
This directive ends at MERGE, not at "PR opened" — so the merge is where the evidence is demanded.

Shape:
  {"pr":123,"checks":{"green":true,"failing":[]},"mergeable":"MERGEABLE",
   "verdict_sha":"<sha the suite passed on>",
   "merge":{"method":"squash","admin":false,"admin_reason":null}}

Record the CI state you OBSERVED, not the state you expect.

assert.else:
A red check is a defect — yours, regardless of which file it points at. Diagnose the mechanism, fix the root cause, re-run the suite on the new sha, push, re-watch. A failure that does not reproduce is not a flake; it is a defect concealing itself.

Admin merge CANNOT bypass this. If it stays red after genuine remediation, park the issue with the evidence and take the next one.
`checks.green` says true but `checks.failing` is non-empty. Resolve the contradiction against `gh pr checks` before merging.

Resolve the conflict by rebasing onto the base and re-verifying — a rebase changes the sha and invalidates the prior pass. A genuinely unresolvable conflict parks the issue.

Admin merge CANNOT bypass a merge conflict: that and a red check are the two cases where it is forbidden outright.
The command passes --admin but the ship record says `admin: false`. Make the record match the action you are taking.

gates._comment: The next issue cannot start until this one is recorded. Catches queue abandonment.
gates.message:
Shape: {"issues":[{"issue":123,"branch":"fix/123-slug","state":"merged|parked|skipped|closed","reason":"<required when parked>","pr":456}]}

The parked log is the one deliverable of an unattended sweep that nobody is awake to read. As a promise in a final report it is unfalsifiable; as a file it is the thing the next branch depends on.

assert.else:
This issue has no terminal state in the queue, so the next issue cannot start.

Parking is a legitimate outcome and never halts the sweep — but an issue left with no recorded state is indistinguishable from one that was quietly abandoned. Record `merged`, `parked` (with a reason), `skipped`, or `closed`.

families._comment: A triage directive. Edits no code, so its gates sit on OUTWARD writes. Repo-scoped, so it needs an explicit disarm.
families.name: triage

gates.message:
Persist the working set BEFORE disposing of anything: one row per issue with # · title · current labels · age · classification · disposition — including the ones you will skip.

A sweep that starts writing before it has enumerated what it is sweeping cannot report at the end which issues it never reached.

gates._comment: The highest-consequence write: this label tells an unattended agent to start writing code, and it does not re-verify.

capture.hint: Pass the issue number positionally (`gh issue edit 1234 --add-label confirmed-bug`) so the gate can require the matching diagnosis.

gates.message:
`confirmed-bug` means "reproduced, root-caused, ready for an agent to write the fix" — and that agent acts on it without re-verifying.

Required sections: Reproduced (evidence — if you did not, this label is wrong) · Root cause (exact file:line) · **Tool calls made** (one line per call: tool -> what it returned) · Introduced by · Blast radius · Coupled symbols · Regression test to write first · Negative space.

The tool-calls section is the point: a grep-only guess shows up as an empty section instead of a confident label.
Same gate as the `gh issue edit` form — routing the label through the API does not change what it authorizes.

Shape: {"entries":[{"issue":123,"slug":"thing.md","written":true}]}  — an empty `entries` array is a valid answer and still gets recorded.

A denied ask whose reasoning exists ONLY in a closed-issue comment is invisible to the next run's prior-denial check, so the same request returns and gets re-litigated from scratch. Recording `{"entries":[]}` is not skipping this step — it is completing it.
